name: Reporting Message
summary: Adversaries may spoof reporting messages in control system environments for evasion and to impair process control. In control systems, reporting messages contain telemetry data (e.g., I/O values) pertaining to the current state of equipment and the industrial process. Reporting messages are important for monitoring the normal operation of a system or identifying important events such as deviations from expected values. If an adversary has the…

analytics.name: Analytic 1879
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a process on an Industrial Control System (ICS) Windows host injecting spoofed reporting messages into the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) data path -- Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) data change notifications with fabricated values, or historian tag writes that override device-sourced values -- from a process that is not the recognized data acquisition process. analytics.name: Analytic 2136
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a Linux process generating Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol unsolicited responses or publishing Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) data changes for device addresses it does not own, from a User Identifier (UID) not associated with the authorized data acquisition service. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect.…

analytics.name: Analytic 2215
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring cross-correlates a field device's reported telemetry against an independent secondary measurement, identifying cases where the reported value diverges from the independent reading while the device's network-layer identity shows a MAC mismatch against its enrolled hardware address. Spoofed reporting messages are, by definition, designed to look protocol-valid.
